subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should the repository accept this grouped set of secret-bearing and code-executing GitHub Action revisions after one coordinated security review, or split the Codex, token, and registry actions for separate validation?
rationale: The diff is mechanically clean, but it changes third-party code running with sensitive credentials and security or release permissions, and repository CODEOWNERS assigns explicit security review to several touched workflows.

options.title: Review and keep grouped
options.body: Have security and CI owners verify the exact upstream revisions and Codex contract, refresh the branch, and merge the group only after relevant checks complete.

options.title: Split sensitive actions
options.body: Move Codex Action, app-token, registry-login, and CodeQL updates into smaller PRs when owners want isolated rollout and rollback evidence.

options.title: Pause the update
options.body: Leave the existing pins in place if the security-sensitive revisions cannot be reviewed or exercised with sufficient confidence.

recommendation.title: Review and keep grouped
recommendation.body: Have security and CI owners verify the exact upstream revisions and Codex contract, refresh the branch, and merge the group only after relevant checks complete.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest person-level history signal spans both Codex-agent workflow creation and repeated release and CI workflow maintenance; the security operations CODEOWNERS team should also review the protected paths.
